```{python}
#| label: fig-resistivity
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Resistivity of silicon at 300 K as a function of the doping concentration, calculated as $\\rho = 1/(q \\mu N)$ with doping-dependent carrier mobilities (Arora mobility fits). p-type silicon has a higher resistivity for the same doping level because of the lower hole mobility."

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

q = 1.602e-19
N = np.logspace(13, 20, 300)   # doping in cm^-3

# Arora mobility fits at 300 K (cm^2/Vs)
mu_n = 92 + 1268 / (1 + (N / 1.3e17) ** 0.91)
mu_p = 54.3 + 406.9 / (1 + (N / 2.35e17) ** 0.88)

rho_n = 1 / (q * mu_n * N)
rho_p = 1 / (q * mu_p * N)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 4))
ax.loglog(N, rho_n, 'b-', lw=2, label='n-type (P, As)')
ax.loglog(N, rho_p, 'r--', lw=2, label='p-type (B)')
ax.set_xlabel('Doping concentration (cm$^{-3}$)')
ax.set_ylabel('Resistivity (Ω cm)')
ax.grid(True, which='both', alpha=0.3)
ax.legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
